slot.brief: A straightforward indefinite integral solved by a single substitution such as u = x² + 1 or a trigonometric substitution; ask for the antiderivative.

stem: A differentiable function $G$ satisfies $G'(x)=\dfrac{6x^2}{x^3+8}$ and $G(0)=0$. For $x>-2$, find $G(x)$.

verdicts.working: Since \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln(x^3+8)=\frac{3x^2}{x^3+8}\), integration gives \(G(x)=2\ln(x^3+8)+C\). Using \(G(0)=0\) yields \(C=-2\ln 8\), so \(G(x)=2\ln\left(\frac{x^3+8}{8}\right)\).

working:
$u=x^3+8,\quad du=3x^2\,dx$.
$G(x)=2\ln(x^3+8)+C$.
$G(0)=0\implies C=-2\ln 8$.
$G(x)=2\ln\left(\dfrac{x^3+8}{8}\right)$.

Independent check: Since \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln(x^3+8)=\frac{3x^2}{x^3+8}\), integration gives \(G(x)=2\ln(x^3+8)+C\). Using \(G(0)=0\) yields \(C=-2\ln 8\), so \(G(x)=2\ln\left(\frac{x^3+8}{8}\right)\).
solution:
Integrating the derivative,
$$G(x)=2\ln(x^3+8)+C.$$
Using $G(0)=0$ gives $C=-2\ln 8$, hence $G(x)=2\ln\left(\dfrac{x^3+8}{8}\right)$.
